content.comment_body: Hi, I use my [product_name] for home automation. When trying to add illuminated pushbuttons, I realized the pushbutton uses - as common and + for the light. Buttons without light work fine by wiring + to common and the input to each button. However, for buttons with light, wiring + to common and - to the light doesn't illuminate it, and using - on common with + on the light prevents a signal from reaching the [product_name]. Is it possible to configure the [product_name] so the inputs respond to - instead of +? For reference, I have a [product_name] [version_no] 24VDC and some expansion modules. Thank you in advance.
Hello, I'm having trouble understanding your wiring setup from the description. If you could share a diagram of the IO connections to your [product_name], I may be able to assist you.
For [product_name] modules with a 24VDC supply, only +24VDC can be connected to the inputs. You may need to adjust your IO wiring to suit the [product_name] or consider using relays. Hope that helps.
[product_name] [version_no] 24VDC modules only work with a positive signal on their inputs.

You could use a pull-up resistor (1 - 10 kOhm) between + and the digital input. Connect the switch between the digital input and the - of the power supply. Note that the input is inverted, so you must adjust the program in your [product_name] to account for this.
Hi, I've attempted to create a wiring layout based on what I understood. Is this correct? Of course, this would involve changing the input in the [product_name] program to reverse the input.
Hi, I've made a diagram of my current wiring where the illumination in the switch isn't working, though the switch itself functions. The light needs to receive +24VDC.
In the future, consider using a [product_name] [version_no] that's designed for AC/DC, allowing for more flexible signal handling. Best regards, [user_name]
If I use a [version_no], could I connect a 24VAC power supply and reverse potential (+/-), enabling all inputs to work with - if set to reverse input?
If you want to control the illumination from the switches, connect the light to the output of the [product_name].

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants experience issues integrating switches with negative common to the [product_name] [version_no] 24VDC module due to its restriction to only accepting positive input signals. This limitation complicates wiring for illuminated switches, often requiring extra components or hardware alternatives. The discussions highlight user confusion over input wiring and confirm that the signal polarity constraint cannot be resolved purely through software configuration.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wishes the [product_name] [version_no] 24VDC module could be set to accept negative input signals, providing greater flexibility in connecting various switch types without needing extra components or reworking the wiring.
pain_keywords: requirement for rewiring or extra components
